title: Serialize concurrent file mutations by realpath (withFileMutationQueue)
wave: Wave 2 — Correctness trên các đường đang ship (W4, W6, W12, W13)
one_line: Add a per-realpath queue that runs one file's mutations one at a time while different files keep running in parallel, and route every tool that writes or deletes a file through it.
user_visible_effect: When two subagents (or two sessions) edit the same file in the same turn, the two writes no longer interleave — the second write is applied cleanly after the first instead of tearing/reordering bytes. Edits to two DIFFERENT files still run concurrently, so no measurable tool latency regression.

files_touched.change: New module exporting `withFileMutationQueue<T>(filePath, fn)`. Module-level `Map<string, Promise<void>>` keyed by realpath, plus a separate `registrationQueue` promise so key resolution is itself serialized. Two-phase handoff via `Promise.withResolvers`, not a bare `tail.then(run)`.

steps.instruction: Create the helper. Port all three load-bearing details from $HOME/Projects/pi-ref/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/file-mutation-queue.ts (read it first, 61 LOC). Import ONLY `realpath` from `node:fs/promises` and `resolve` from `node:path`. Do NOT import anything from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` — see risk: the barrel pulls the native addon and makes the test unrunnable. Implement `isMissingPathError` inline (check `code === "ENOENT" || code === "ENOTDIR"`) exactly as the reference does, rather than importing `isEnoent`/`isEnotdir`. Adapt the reference's `new Promise<void>((resolveQueue) => { releaseNext = resolveQueue; })` to `Promise.withResolvers<void>()` per AGENTS.md (repo precedent: packages/coding-agent/src/advisor/runtime.ts:454).

Key the queue by `await realpath(resolve(filePath))`, falling back to `resolve(filePath)` ONLY when realpath rejects with ENOENT or ENOTDIR; rethrow every other error (e.g. EACCES, ELOOP). This is detail 1 of 3 — a resolve-only key silently fails to serialize two agents that reach one file through a symlink or a `..` segment. Keep `getMutationQueueKey` as a separate named function so the fallback is one readable branch.

Serialize the REGISTRATION itself through a module-level `let registrationQueue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve()`. Each call does `const registration = registrationQueue.then(async () => { ...resolve key, read currentQueue, build nextQueue, set map... })`, then reassigns `registrationQueue = registration.then(() => undefined, () => undefined)` BEFORE awaiting. This is detail 2 of 3 — without it two concurrent `realpath` awaits can both read the same `currentQueue` and both append to it, which is precisely the race the separate queue exists to prevent. The `.then(ok, err)` two-arg form is required: a plain `.then(() => undefined)` would leave `registrationQueue` permanently rejected and deadlock every later call after one throw.

Implement the two-phase handoff, NOT `tail.then(run)`. Inside the registration callback create `nextQueue` with `Promise.withResolvers<void>()`, store `chainedQueue = currentQueue.then(() => nextQueue.promise)` in the map, and return `{ key, currentQueue, chainedQueue, releaseNext: nextQueue.resolve }`. After awaiting the registration: `await currentQueue`, then `try { return await fn(); } finally { releaseNext(); if (fileMutationQueues.get(key) === chainedQueue) fileMutationQueues.delete(key); }`. The `finally` is what makes a THROWING mutation release the queue — a plain chain would wedge the key forever and hang every later mutation of that file. The identity check before delete is what stops a late finisher from evicting a successor that already chained onto it.

Route the shared seam. Wrap the entire body of `writeFileWithFallback` (:402) in `withFileMutationQueue(dst, async () => { ...existing body... })`, and do the same for `deleteFileWithFallback` (:305). This single edit covers three of the four mutating tools: `edit` create/update (via `createEditWritethrough` -> lsp/writethrough.ts:314), `edit` move destination (edit/index.ts:674), and `write` (write.ts:909-911 -> lsp/writethrough.ts:314). Delete must go through the SAME queue as write — a delete landing on top of a concurrent write is exactly the lost-update this item exists to stop, which is why :305 is in scope even though the plan only names the write path. Keep `fallbackHandlers` / `deleteFallbackHandlers` iteration and the `logger.warn` handler-throw catch exactly as they are; the queue must not swallow or reorder handler behavior.

Route `ast_edit` explicitly. `grep -c writeFileWithFallback packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ast-edit.ts` is 0, so step 5 does NOT cover this tool — do not assume the chokepoint reached it. Wrap the applying `astEdit({...})` calls. Because one call can rewrite many files under a glob, see open_questions: the defensible default is to key on the tool's resolved target scope (`resolvedSearchPath`) so two `ast_edit` calls on the same scope serialize while calls on disjoint scopes stay parallel. Do NOT wrap the `dryRun: true` preview call at :285 — it only parses and must not take the write lock.

Write the 5 contract tests described in test_contract. Use `bun:test` (`describe`/`expect`/`it`), `node:fs/promises` for fixtures, and `os.tmpdir()` + `fs.mkdtemp` for a real temp dir. Import the helper by its module path. Do NOT use `mock.module()`, do NOT source-grep, do NOT mutate `process.env` or `Bun.*` at file scope. Clean the temp dir in `afterEach`.

Add one line under `## [Unreleased]` -> `### Fixed`: user-facing phrasing, e.g. 'Fixed concurrent edits to the same file by parallel agents interleaving instead of applying cleanly.' No issue link unless a real internal issue number exists. Do not touch any already-released section.

test_contract: The contract defended is: "mutations to one file apply one-at-a-time; mutations to different files still overlap." A regression makes concurrent agents silently clobber or tear each other's writes — the user sees a file whose content is neither edit, with no error anywhere. Specifically: (1) two concurrent mutations on the SAME path must not interleave — assert the observed order is strictly before/after with no overlap (each task pushes 'start', awaits a tick, pushes 'end'; assert no 'start' appears between another task's 'start' and 'end'); (2) two mutations on DIFFERENT paths MUST overlap — assert they do, because a single global queue is a performance regression disguised as a fix, and this is the assertion that keeps the Map honestly keyed; (3) a symlink and its target share ONE queue entry, which is what the realpath key buys and what a resolve-only key silently misses; (4) a not-yet-created file does NOT throw (ENOENT/ENOTDIR falls back to resolve); (5) double registration — two mutations arriving while the first is still resolving its key must still chain, not both read the same predecessor and run concurrently.

gate:
Two independent assertions, both able to go red.

(1) TYPE GATE: `bun run check:ts` exits 0. Goes red on a type error, a missing top-level import, a `ReturnType<>`, or a format violation (it runs the formatter check across 5445 files). Verified meaningful: it is green now, so any new red is caused by this change.

(2) BEHAVIOR GATE: `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tools/file-mutation-queue.test.ts` reports 5 pass / 0 fail, once the addon is built. Test 2 (different paths MUST overlap) is the gate that can actually fail on a wrong implementation: the naive single-global-tail port makes it red. Test 5 (double registration) is the gate for detail 2: drop `registrationQueue` and it goes red. Test 3 (symlink shares an entry) is the gate for detail 1: swap realpath for plain `resolve` and it goes red. Any single one of the three going red is a real W12 defect, not a flake.

COVERAGE GATE: `git grep -c writeFileWithFallback packages/coding-agent/src/tools/ast-edit.ts` still returns 0, confirming ast_edit was routed explicitly and NOT silently assumed covered.
gate_can_fail: Yes. check:ts was observed green at baseline (16/16 packages Done) on this exact HEAD, so it is a live gate, not a no-op. The 5 behavior tests each target a distinct defect: a naive single-global-tail port fails test 2; dropping the serialized registration fails test 5; a resolve-only key fails test 3; missing ENOENT fallback fails test 4; a non-`finally` release wedges test 1. The tests are runnable once `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build` succeeds, which I verified is the only blocker (a bare `bun test` of a node-builtins-only module in this repo passes 1/1 today).
effort: M — one new helper (~60 LOC), two modified call-path files, one new test file. The plan's estimate holds. The extra work versus a naive port is the `deleteFileWithFallback` wrap (step 5) and the `ast_edit` fan-out keying decision (step 6), neither of which the plan spells out.
risk: Highest risk is a RE-ENTRANT call deadlocking the queue. Wrapping `writeFileWithFallback` (:402) puts the lock around the whole fallback-handler loop (:440-452), which invokes extension-registered handlers from `addFileWriteFallback` (wired at packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/runner.ts:778, exposed as `registerFileWriteFallback` at extensibility/extensions/types.ts:1379). If any such handler calls back into `writeFileWithFallback` or `deleteFileWithFallback` for the same path, the queue never releases and that path hangs forever. The queue is NOT reentrant — there is no owner token. Second-highest: `ast_edit` fans out over many files per call, so per-file keying has no single key to use. Third: do not let the new module import the `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` barrel (verified: it drags in the native addon and makes the test unrunnable in this environment).
open_questions: DECISION REQUIRED — extension surface. `withFileMutationQueue` is internal: an out-of-repo extension registering a tool via `registerTool` (packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/extensions/types.ts:1347) and calling `Bun.write` directly bypasses the queue entirely. pi-ref RESOLVED this by exporting `withFileMutationQueue` on its public surface (see $HOME/Projects/pi-ref/packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts:120 and src/index.ts:376). omp must pick deliberately: (a) export it from the extension API now, or (b) record in the M2 handoff that third-party mutations are not serialized, with a reason. The answer MUST be written into the M2 handoff — M2 must not have to guess. Note the plan's cited anchor types.ts:1322 is wrong (that is an `on("auto_compaction_end")` overload); `registerTool` is at :1347.

DECISION REQUIRED — ast_edit fan-out keying. One `ast_edit` call can rewrite MANY files under a glob (runAstEditTargets loops at :85-95). Options: (a) key on the resolved scope path (`resolvedSearchPath`) — coarse but cheap, and two ast_edit calls on the same scope serialize; (b) key per rewritten file — impossible today, because the writes happen inside the native `astEdit` call and omp never sees them individually; (c) do not route ast_edit and accept the gap. Recommend (a) and document the coarseness. The plan asserts ast_edit must be routed but does not say how to key it.

VERIFY BEFORE CODING — read-modify-write atomicity. `edit`'s update path reads the file at packages/coding-agent/src/edit/index.ts:711 (`preWriteBytes = await Bun.file(request.path).bytes()`) and compares after writing (~:735-747, throwing 'edit appeared successful but file content did not change'). If the queue is entered at :402, that read at :711 is OUTSIDE the lock, so two agents can still read the same pre-image and the second write silently discards the first — the queue prevents interleaving and byte-tearing but NOT lost updates. Decide whether W12 claims to fix only interleaving (defensible, matches the plan's wording) or also lost updates (which needs the lock moved up to the `#write` callback at edit/index.ts:495, the single funnel for ALL edit ops). State the chosen scope explicitly in the PR.

CONFIRM SCOPE — what `concurrency = "exclusive"` already covers. BOTH `EditTool` (edit/index.ts:328) and `WriteTool` (tools/write.ts:441) already declare `readonly concurrency = "exclusive"`. I traced its implementation: packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts:3589-3611 chains exclusive tools via a FUNCTION-LOCAL `lastExclusive` declared at :3511 inside `executeToolCalls` (which starts at :3024) — so it serializes tool calls WITHIN ONE agent's single batch, and is NOT shared across agents or sessions. That is why W12 is still needed (the plan's premise holds: subagents are in-process via createAgentSession in task/executor.ts:3960, no spawn, so they share the module-level Map). But the PR should say so, or a reviewer will ask why both mechanisms are needed. Note `ast_edit` declares NO concurrency (name at :152, no `concurrency` field), so it defaults to shared and gets no agent-loop protection at all.

OPTIONAL — queue map hygiene. The reference implementation deletes its Map entry on release, so the Map stays proportional to CONCURRENTLY-mutated files, not to files ever touched. Preserve that; a Map that only ever grows is a slow leak in a long session.
